chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: A liquid unknown displays a very broad, intense IR absorption band centered at 3350 cm-1. What functional group is present?
questions.correct_answer: Alcohol (O-H stretch)
questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding broadens the O-H stretch significantly in liquid films.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: An unknown compound shows a sharp, strong IR peak at 1715 cm-1. Which compound matches this spectrum?
questions.correct_answer: Cyclohexanone (unconjugated 6-ring ketone)
questions.explanation: Unconjugated 6-membered cyclic ketones absorb strongly near 1715 cm-1.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: How can an ester be distinguished from a ketone using infrared spectroscopy?

options.label: B
options.text: Esters show a C=O stretch at higher frequency (~1735-1750 cm-1) and strong C-O single bond stretches near 1200 cm-1

options.label: C
options.text: Esters lack a C=O stretch entirely

options.label: D
options.text: Ketones show broad absorptions at 3300 cm-1

questions.correct_answer: Esters show a C=O stretch at higher frequency (~1735-1750 cm-1) and strong C-O single bond stretches near 1200 cm-1
questions.explanation: Esters feature an inductive shift pushing C=O higher and prominent C-O-C stretches.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.topic: IR alkyne C-H vs alkene C-H
questions.question: Where does the sp C-H stretch of a terminal alkyne appear in an IR spectrum?
questions.correct_answer: Sharp absorption near 3300 cm-1
questions.explanation: Higher s-character strengthens the sp C-H bond, shifting its stretch to 3300 cm-1.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: In the mass spectrum of 2-butanone (C4H8O, MW 72), what does the peak at m/z = 72 represent?

options.label: B
options.text: The base peak formed by alpha-cleavage

options.label: C
options.text: The molecular ion (M+•) formed by loss of a single electron

questions.correct_answer: The molecular ion (M+•) formed by loss of a single electron
questions.explanation: The intact radical cation resulting from initial electron bombardment corresponds to MW = 72.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: In the mass spectrum of 2-butanone (CH3COCH2CH3), what is the origin of the base peak at m/z = 43?

options.label: B
options.text: Loss of CO to form propyl radical

options.label: C
options.text: Alpha-cleavage of an ethyl radical to yield the acetylium ion [CH3C≡O]+

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of a methyl radical to form [CH3CH2C≡O]+ at m/z 57

questions.correct_answer: Alpha-cleavage of an ethyl radical to yield the acetylium ion [CH3C≡O]+
questions.explanation: Loss of the larger ethyl radical produces the stabilized acylium ion at m/z = 43.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: An organic halide shows twin molecular ion peaks at m/z = 156 and m/z = 158 in a 1:1 intensity ratio. What halogen is present?

options.label: D
options.text: One bromine atom (79Br and 81Br in 50.7% : 49.3% natural abundance)

questions.correct_answer: One bromine atom (79Br and 81Br in 50.7% : 49.3% natural abundance)
questions.explanation: Bromine's two stable isotopes occur in equal abundance, creating a 1:1 M/(M+2) signature.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: An unknown shows molecular ion peaks at m/z = 112 and m/z = 114 in a 3:1 intensity ratio. What halogen is present?

options.label: B
options.text: One chlorine atom (35Cl and 37Cl in 75.8% : 24.2% natural abundance)

questions.correct_answer: One chlorine atom (35Cl and 37Cl in 75.8% : 24.2% natural abundance)
questions.explanation: Chlorine exhibits a characteristic 3:1 M/(M+2) intensity ratio.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which structural feature is required for a carbonyl compound to undergo a McLafferty rearrangement in mass spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: A hydrogen atom on the gamma (γ) carbon relative to the carbonyl group

options.label: D
options.text: A double bond conjugated with the carbonyl

questions.correct_answer: A hydrogen atom on the gamma (γ) carbon relative to the carbonyl group
questions.explanation: McLafferty fragmentation proceeds via a 6-membered cyclic transition state requiring a gamma-hydrogen.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Mass Spectrometry and Infrared Spectroscopy
questions.question: How can an aliphatic nitrile (R-C≡N) be distinguished from an internal alkyne (R-C≡C-R) in IR spectroscopy?

options.label: A
options.text: Nitriles show a strong/medium peak at 2250 cm-1; symmetric internal alkynes show no C≡C peak due to zero dipole change

options.label: D
options.text: Nitriles have broad peaks at 3400 cm-1

questions.correct_answer: Nitriles show a strong/medium peak at 2250 cm-1; symmetric internal alkynes show no C≡C peak due to zero dipole change
questions.explanation: Symmetric alkynes have no net dipole moment change during vibration and are IR inactive.
